panels.description: Number of distinct repositories that had at least one successful production deploy reported to a webhook whose project does not map that repository, in the selected time range. Anything above 0 means a pipeline is still tagged with an old team: fix the pipeline's team/webhook and the count drops to 0 on the next collection. Repos are matched on normalized URLs (case, trailing slash and '.git' ignored).

targets.rawSql:
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT regexp_replace(lower(t.repo_url), '/?(\.git)?/?$', '')) AS repos_affected
FROM (
  SELECT dc.repo_url
  FROM cicd_deployment_commits dc
  JOIN project_mapping pm ON pm."table" = 'cicd_scopes' AND pm.row_id = dc.cicd_scope_id
  WHERE dc.environment = 'PRODUCTION' AND dc.result = 'SUCCESS'
    AND $__timeFilter(dc.finished_date)
    AND NOT EXISTS (
      SELECT 1 FROM project_mapping rm
      JOIN repos r ON r.id = rm.row_id
      WHERE rm."table" = 'repos' AND rm.project_name = pm.project_name
        AND regexp_replace(lower(dc.repo_url), '/?(\.git)?/?$', '') = regexp_replace(lower(r.url), '/?(\.git)?/?$', '')
    )
) t

panels.title: Repos affected (range)

panels.description: Successful production deploys whose webhook belongs to a project that does not map the deployed repository. A non-empty result almost always means a pipeline is still tagged with an old team after an ownership change, so the deploy (and the PRs it ships first) is credited to that old team. Fix the pipeline's team/webhook; rows disappear once no such deploy falls in the time range. The repo_projects column lists the projects that currently map the repo; an empty value means the repo is mapped to no project or its URL does not resolve to a repo. Repos are matched on normalized URLs (case, trailing slash and '.git' ignored).

defaults.noValue: No production deploy on a non-owning webhook in this range

targets.rawSql:
SELECT dc.finished_date AS "time", pm.project_name AS webhook_team, (SELECT string_agg(DISTINCT rm.project_name, ', ' ORDER BY rm.project_name) FROM project_mapping rm JOIN repos r ON r.id = rm.row_id WHERE rm."table" = 'repos' AND regexp_replace(lower(r.url), '/?(\.git)?/?$', '') = regexp_replace(lower(dc.repo_url), '/?(\.git)?/?$', '')) AS repo_projects, dc.repo_url, dc.cicd_scope_id, dc.commit_sha
FROM cicd_deployment_commits dc
JOIN project_mapping pm ON pm."table" = 'cicd_scopes' AND pm.row_id = dc.cicd_scope_id
WHERE dc.environment = 'PRODUCTION' AND dc.result = 'SUCCESS'
  AND $__timeFilter(dc.finished_date)
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM project_mapping rm
    JOIN repos r ON r.id = rm.row_id
    WHERE rm."table" = 'repos' AND rm.project_name = pm.project_name
      AND regexp_replace(lower(dc.repo_url), '/?(\.git)?/?$', '') = regexp_replace(lower(r.url), '/?(\.git)?/?$', '')
  )
ORDER BY dc.finished_date DESC

panels.title: Production deploys on a webhook whose project does not map the repo

panels.description: Deployed PRs divided by distinct production deployments, per week, across all projects. Values above 2 (red band) mean batches of PRs are being attached to single deploys: typically a repo's first deploy on a new webhook back-linking its whole history, or a repo that releases rarely. Check project_pr_metrics for the deployment_commit_id with the most PRs in that week.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT $__timeGroup(ppm.pr_deployed_date, '7d') AS "time",
       CAST(COUNT(*) AS NUMERIC) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT ppm.deployment_commit_id), 0) AS prs_per_deploy
FROM project_pr_metrics ppm
WHERE ppm.pr_deployed_date IS NOT NULL AND $__timeFilter(ppm.pr_deployed_date)
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

panels.title: PRs per production deploy, weekly
